question: In chronic osteomyelitis with a radiologically confirmed sequestrum, prolonged high-dose intravenous antibiotics alone can sterilise the sequestrum and render operative sequestrectomy unnecessary.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The sequestrum is avascular — it has no blood supply. Antibiotics are delivered via the bloodstream and cannot penetrate tissue that lacks vascularity. No antibiotic regimen, however intensive, can sterilise a sequestrum. Operative removal is mandatory.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. The sequestrum is avascular dead bone. Antibiotics require a functioning blood supply to reach their target tissue. Because the sequestrum has no blood supply, no concentration of antibiotic (however high or prolonged) can penetrate it. Sequestrectomy is therefore always required once a sequestrum is established.
